name: across-2
statement: The 10-13 points that Olmo-3.1 RL holds over the cued base are mostly a learned token-budget controller, trained by 3.1's scoring of truncated rollouts as failures, that keeps self-checking ('Wait') on answers that are short for the budget and forces convergence before the 16k cap on long ones, written into the weights as a low-rank late-layer stop/deliberation readout; it is not new mathematical skill, so the gap sits in cap hits and long problems, every recovering transplant takes RL's length, and Olmo-3.0 RL (truncation masked) is close to the cued base.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base, Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math and Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0) on MATH-500 and the 328 at cap 16,384, T 0.6 and T 1.0, and weight interpolation base + a*(RL - base) for a in [0, 1.5]. Does not claim the controller explains the base's loops at T 0.6 (a sampling effect) or the 'Answer:' format change.

explains.quote: not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: Only 3.1 got a reward signal against running past the budget, the training pressure that builds a budget controller.

explains.quote: So on their pair the cue already equals RL on MATH-500
explains.how: Olmo-3.0 RL, trained with truncation masked, gains nothing over the cued base: without the budget penalty there is no gap.
At equal mean tokens RL converts cap hits into finished answers: same budget, better allocation.
RL does not spend more tokens on the 328; it distributes the same budget across problems differently.

explains.quote: By RL-length quartile (82 each) base/RL right: 78/82, 52/67, 30/45, 4/12
explains.how: The gap grows with problem length, where budget control decides the outcome.

explains.quote: T1 cap hits exceed T2's by 15.2 points in Q4
explains.how: At T 1.0 on MATH-500 the longest quartile's gap is cap hits, the budget failure mode.

explains.quote: Median tokens of right answers: base 1,432, RL 3,014
explains.how: On ordinary problems RL deliberates longer before committing, the short-answer side of the controller, which catches slips.

explains.quote: RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 % of 473 answers
explains.how: Where the base stops, RL often declines to stop: a changed stop readout.
RL's largest early differences on cap-hit problems are deliberation-control tokens, not math content.

explains.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
explains.how: The concentrated low-rank part of the delta reads out as the controller's vocabulary in late layers.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Accuracy and length move together across transplant arms, as expected if the gain is the length controller.

explains.quote: Their small RL recalibration 'mainly taught the model to commit and stop'
explains.how: In another model RL's effect on MATH-500 is also commit/stop control under a token cap.

explains.quote: on a cap-limited model a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain
explains.how: On cap-limited models, accuracy is governed by finishing under the cap, the quantity the controller sets.
Dosing a fine-tune delta moves stop behaviour monotonically, the signature of a scalar stop readout along the delta.

conflicts.quote: RL leads the cued base by 5-12 points
conflicts.how: Olmo-3.0 RL beats the cued base by 5-12 points on harder sets (AMC, AIME, OlympiadBench) in Wang et al., so 3.0 is not equal to the cued base everywhere; the theory must attribute this to their 31,744 cap or contamination (AIME 2022-23 overlap).
37 of the 65 RL-only items are content errors, not cap hits; the theory needs RL's extra self-checking to catch them, which is not shown.

conflicts.quote: MLP layers 0-15 carry about twice what 16-31 do
conflicts.how: Most of the KL to RL is closed by early layers, not by a late-layer readout.

conflicts.quote: The best set sits in layers 1-15
conflicts.how: Attribution-ranked neurons are early, though layer 31 is also named.

conflicts.quote: past ~1.5 answers run to the token cap
conflicts.how: Extrapolating an RL delta past a=1.5 made answers run to the cap in a code pair, the opposite of this theory's prediction 4.

rival: Self-copy suppression in layers 0-15 (across-1), or genuine new math skill spread evenly over problems. Separation: (1) Olmo-3.0 RL-Zero-Math in our harness: this theory predicts it scores near the cued base with many cap hits; the skill rival predicts near 3.1. (2) Layer split: this theory predicts the RL delta of layers 16-31 removes more cap hits than that of layers 0-15; across-1 predicts the reverse. (3) Extrapolation a=1.5: this theory predicts fewer cap hits than RL; a generic-overshoot rival predicts runaway to the cap.

predictions.experiment: allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, the 328, one sample, cap 16,384, grader v3: right
predictions.refuted_by: Right >= 200 (3.0 matches 3.1's 206 without the truncation penalty)

predictions.experiment: Same 3.0 run on the 328: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits <= 25 (3.0 already finishes within budget like 3.1's 20)

predictions.experiment: Base + RL delta in layers 16-31 only (rest base), opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits >= 95, or the layers 0-15 arm has fewer cap hits than this arm

predictions.experiment: Base + 1.5*(RL - base), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, the 328, cap 16,384, grader v3: cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: Cap hits >= 40 (answers run away to the cap instead of converging earlier)

predictions.experiment: Base + 0.5*(RL - base), opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: right (with mean tokens per problem expected between the base's 3,933 and RL's 4,694)
predictions.refuted_by: Right >= 455 while mean tokens per problem stay <= 4,000 (the gain arrives without the length change)
